_about: Icebreakers. groupMin/groupMax = how many campers it works for. sayIt = the English everyone must say out loud, per level.

icebreakers.name: Two Truths and a Lie
steps: Each person thinks of three facts about themselves. Two are true, one is a lie.
One by one, say your three facts out loud.
The group votes on which one is the lie.
Reveal the answer. Guessers who got it right earn a point.

middle: I think number ___ is the lie.
confident: I'm pretty sure that's the lie because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Beginners can hold up three picture cards instead of writing.

icebreakers.name: Picture Scavenger Hunt
materials: Picture list (no words) for each team
Phones or paper to check items off
steps: Give each team a list made only of pictures: a red thing, something round, a leaf, etc.
Teams find each item in the room or outside.
To check off an item, the team must say its name in English.
First team to finish (with every word said out loud) wins.

middle: We found a ___ next to the ___.
confident: We found a ___. It was hard because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Confident speakers can describe where they found each item.

icebreakers.name: Name and Move
steps: Stand in a circle.
Say your name and one thing you like, with a move that shows it.
The whole group repeats your name, your sentence and your move.
Go around until everyone has had a turn. Then try to say everyone's names.

middle: I'm ___ and I love ___ because it's fun.

icebreakers.levelTip: Great first-day activity: no reading needed at all.

icebreakers.name: Would You Rather
materials: Two signs: one for each side of the room
steps: Read a question with two choices, like 'pizza or rice?'
Everyone walks to the side of the room for their choice.
A few people from each side say why out loud.
Anyone can switch sides if they hear a good reason.

confident: I'd pick ___, but I understand why people like ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: For beginners, show the two choices as pictures.

icebreakers.name: Find Someone Who
materials: Bingo cards with 'Find someone who…' boxes
steps: Each person gets a bingo card: 'Find someone who plays soccer', 'speaks three languages'…
Walk around and ask questions out loud.
When someone says yes, they sign that box.
First to get a full line shouts 'Bingo!' and reads the names.
icebreakers.levelTip: Use picture boxes for a beginner version.

icebreakers.name: Paper Snowball Fight
materials: One sheet of paper per person
steps: Everyone writes an answer to a fun question, like 'My favorite food is…'.
Crumple the paper into a snowball.
Snowball fight for 30 seconds!
Pick up a snowball, read it out loud, and guess who wrote it.

middle: This says ___. I think ___ wrote it.

icebreakers.levelTip: Keep the question simple and the snowball fight short.

icebreakers.name: Where I'm From Line
materials: A big world map, or tape on the floor as a map
steps: Lay out a world map or a tape map on the floor.
Everyone stands on a place that matters to them.
Each person says one sentence about that place.
Others can ask one question.

middle: I'm from ___. The food there is ___.
confident: I grew up in ___. Something I miss is ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Let students choose any place: home, a city they love, a dream trip.

icebreakers.name: Name That Song
materials: Short clips of songs the students choose (check them first)
steps: Before camp, ask students for one song they love from home or from now.
Play 10 seconds of a song.
Teams guess who picked it and say one word about how it sounds.
The person who picked it tells the group about it.

middle: This song sounds ___. I think ___ picked it.
confident: This song reminds me of ___ because ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Use their world: songs from home and current hits both count.

icebreakers.name: Draw It, Say It
steps: One player from each team picks a word card.
They draw it without letters or numbers.
Their team shouts guesses in English.
The first team to say the exact word gets the point.

confident: It could be a ___, or maybe a ___.

icebreakers.levelTip: Pull word cards from today's topic to warm up the key words.

icebreakers.name: Human Knot with Directions
steps: Stand in a tight circle and grab two different hands across the circle.
Untangle the knot without letting go.
The only rule: you must give directions in English.
Time each team. Try again and beat your time.

confident: If you go under there, we can turn around.

icebreakers.levelTip: Good warm-up before the Riding the bus activity (left, right, stop).
